summary: Configured daily log rotation for /var/log/inventory/app.log on node1 via /etc/logrotate.d/inventory-app (daily, rotate 7, compress, delaycompress, copytruncate) so the app can keep writing to the same inode after rotation. Validated syntax with `logrotate -d`, then forced two real rotations to prove: (1) copytruncate preserves the file's inode so a writer never loses its file handle, (2) compressed rotations accumulate correctly (.1 -> .2.gz) with delaycompress deferring compression by one cycle, consistent with a 7-rotation retention policy. Reset the log directory to a clean baseline afterward. Completed the mandatory single-node restart protocol: captured boot_id baseline, issued `systemctl reboot` via a backgrounded ack-then-disconnect wrapper, polled through the outage, confirmed boot_id changed (636556ce... -> 3e7264d8...) and uptime-since reset to 08:26:09, then verified post-reboot that the logrotate config file, the log file/content, and the logrotate.timer (active+enabled, next run scheduled) all recovered intact.
actions_performed: Inspected /var/log/inventory/app.log and confirmed no live logrotate.d entry existed for it
Created /etc/logrotate.d/inventory-app with daily rotation, rotate 7, compress, delaycompress, missingok, notifempty, copytruncate
Forced a rotation with `logrotate -f -v` and confirmed app.log kept the same inode (copytruncate) after truncation
Appended new content to app.log post-rotation and forced a second rotation, confirming the previous .1 file was compressed to .2.gz and new content was captured, proving continuous writability
Cleaned up test rotation artifacts and reset app.log to its original baseline content
Confirmed logrotate.timer is enabled/active and scheduled to run logrotate.service daily
Captured pre-restart boot_id and service/config baseline on node1
Issued a backgrounded systemctl reboot on node1 so the exec call could acknowledge before disconnection
Polled node1 until exec calls succeeded again, observing connection timeouts/reset then success
Verified boot_id and uptime-since changed, proving an actual reboot occurred
Re-verified logrotate config, log file/content, and logrotate.timer status post-reboot

evidence.requirement: Daily rotation with 7 compressed rotations retained, app can keep writing after rotation (copytruncate)
evidence.summary: Created /etc/logrotate.d/inventory-app (daily, rotate 7, compress, delaycompress, copytruncate), validated syntax, then forced two rotations proving inode preservation (writability continues) and correct compressed rotation chaining (.1 -> .2.gz).

evidence.requirement: Rotation is actually scheduled to run (daily cadence enforced by the system, not just config text)
evidence.summary: logrotate.timer confirmed active and enabled with a scheduled next run both before and after the node restart.

evidence.requirement: Healthy pre-restart baseline captured on node1
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id 636556ce-a308-49cc-b873-62cedb1c077d, uptime-since 08:24:55, logrotate config contents, log directory state, and log content prior to reboot.
Backgrounded `systemctl reboot` (delayed 2s, nohup+disown) returned 'reboot scheduled' successfully before the node went unreachable.

evidence.requirement: Node1 restart proven via changed boot identity
evidence.summary: Polling showed connection timeout/reset during the outage, then a successful reconnection with boot_id changed to 3e7264d8-0f2a-4310-89c2-aa7e70d45117 and uptime-since reset to 08:26:09, proving an actual reboot occurred.

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of required config/data on node1
evidence.summary: After reboot, /etc/logrotate.d/inventory-app content, /var/log/inventory/app.log content, and logrotate.timer active/enabled status all verified intact, plus a fresh `logrotate -d` debug run confirming the config still parses correctly.
